info.title: ProductManager API
info.description: Roadmap & market-simulation system. The REST API is the only write path: the web app, the CLI and the MCP server are all clients of this contract.

delete.summary: Refused while simulation runs still reference the set — a run must stay reproducible.

post.summary:
Branches the set: a new set with a deep copy of every parameter and a pointer back here.
The branch is fully independent — editing it never touches the parent.

put.summary:
Sets (upserting) one parameter. Supply `clientSegmentId` + `flowKind`
(+ `moduleProductId` for CrossSellRate) for a parameter the engine reads — that triple
is the engine's own parameter key, so writing it twice replaces rather than duplicates.
Supply `key` instead for a free-form assumption the engine ignores.

post.summary: Exchanges the configured single-user password for a bearer token.

get.summary: Echoes the authenticated subject — a cheap way for clients to check their token.

post.summary:
Runs the fit synchronously: maps the ledger as of the date onto the calibration contract,
executes the pure calibration module, stores the run, and creates the fitted assumption set.

delete.summary: Deleting is the only write a stored fit allows — it is never edited.

get.summary: Prior vs posterior for every parameter the fit touched, and the reason for each one it could not.
The exact calibration input this run was executed against — priors plus the observations as of the date.

put.summary: Sets (upserting by segment) how much of a segment this channel reaches and originates.
Sets (upserting by product) this channel's signed bias toward a product.

Replaces the segment's observed starting state — the stocks and unit economics the
simulation engine starts a run from.
Sets (upserting by module) one module's starting penetration and pricing in this segment.

Sets (upserting by approach) the share of this segment's firms on one approach to a process
— e.g. 99% settling via the incumbent utility, 1% on chain. Effective coverage is weighted by
this mix, which is what stops "gold on the 1% approach" from reading as gold.

delete.summary: Deleting a competitor is refused while its products still exist — they are market evidence.

get.summary:
The covariate's observed history, read out of the facts ledger. `knownAsOf` reconstructs
what we knew at a past instant; where a reading was later corrected for the same effective
date, the latest recorded value wins.

post.summary:
Records a coverage assessment, upserting on the (product, process, approach?, segment?) key.
That tuple *is* the identity of an assessment — re-posting it re-assesses the same row (200)
rather than leaving two contradictory answers to the same question behind (201 on first write).
Uniqueness is enforced here rather than by a unique index because two of the four key columns
are nullable, and SQL treats NULLs as distinct.

put.summary: Re-assesses one coverage row by id. The key dimensions are immutable — post to move them.

post.summary:
Appends one observation. The recorded date is stamped server-side unless the caller supplies
`recordedAt` — the import/backfill path, for history whose "when we learned it" is
genuinely in the past. A recorded date in the future is refused.
            


With a `source`, the append is repeat-safe: the source event already bound to a materially
identical fact returns that fact (200); bound to a different one, it is refused as a correction.
Either way nothing is appended — the ledger is never rewritten.
Adds one delta to the feature's market meaning.

put.summary: Replaces the feature's whole delta set.

post.summary:
Creates an edge. With `sources`, an already-bound source record returns its edge (200)
instead, binding any listed records not bound yet.

Imports a whole roster into one market in a single call, relationships included. Items without
a source match by natural key (market, name), so re-importing the same roster corrects it
rather than duplicating it. Items with a source match by source identity, update only what
they carry, and report per item what happened — see ProductManager.Api.Contracts.FirmImportItem. One item's
exception never stops the others; everything that applies is saved together.

Fills every segment's measured stocks with deterministically generated synthetic firms, so a firm-level simulation runs over the whole market and not only the part we happen to have names for. Regeneration replaces the previous synthetic population: identities are hashes of (market, segment, role, index), so running this twice is a no-op rather than a doubling.

Creates the edge. The edge is symmetric, so (A, B) and (B, A) are the same integration and
the second one is a conflict rather than a second row — two rows would let the same pair
carry two different quality scores.

delete.summary: Deletes the market and everything hanging off it (segments, processes, products, firms).

post.summary:
Opens an opportunity. With a `source` already bound, returns the bound opportunity (200)
instead — the unique binding index makes this safe under retries.
Adds a business process to the scope (idempotent). Refused once the deal is decided.
Qualifies the opportunity; repeating the same qualification is a 200 no-op.

Decides the opportunity and appends the ledger entry that calibration will later read. The
two writes are one transaction: a decision that never reached the ledger would silently
disappear from every future fit.
            


Repeat-safe: the identical decision again (a retry after a lost response) returns 200 and
appends nothing; a different one is refused as a correction, leaving the recorded decision and
its fact untouched.

put.summary: Upserts pricing for the product; a null segment sets the default price.

delete.summary: Drops a price row. Omit the segment to drop the product's default price.

post.summary: Declares that this project cannot start before another project finishes.

put.summary: Upserts the effort this project demands from a team in a period. Zero points clears it.

post.summary: Links a feature this project delivers — the one join between execution and market sides.
Makes this roadmap the workspace's live plan, retiring whichever was live before.
Plans (or re-plans) a project on this roadmap.

put.summary: Moves a planned project on the timeline — the drag-and-drop reschedule.

delete.summary: Removes a project from this roadmap.

put.summary:
Rewrites the display order: each project's sort order becomes its index in the posted list.
The list must name exactly the projects planned on this roadmap.

post.summary: Branches this roadmap into a scenario: a new, non-live roadmap with a deep copy of the plan.
Adopts a scenario branch into this (live) roadmap — the merge back to main.

get.summary:
Team-capacity overallocations and dependency-ordering violations for this roadmap.
Capacity is a feasibility constraint: demand above capacity in a period is flagged, never
silently accepted.

post.summary:
Maps the workspace's observed market state onto the engine contract, runs it synchronously,
and stores the run with its full input snapshot and result.

delete.summary: Deletes a run. Deleting is the only write a stored run allows — it is never edited.

get.summary:
The run's trajectories: per-segment and total bands (mean/P10/P50/P90) plus the NPV
distribution. Firm-level runs carry an extra `diagnostics` property here (the same
document `GET {id}/diagnostics` returns); the trajectory fields are identical in both
modes, which is what lets a comparison put an aggregate run and a firm-level run side by side.

Firm-level diagnostics: opportunity funnels by segment and by channel, average sales-cycle
length, scope expansions, the mean utility gap on lost deals, and how many synthetic firms
the run created. 404 on an aggregate run — it has no opportunities to count.

The exact engine input this run was executed against. Re-running the engine on this document
alone — no database reads — reproduces the stored result byte for byte.

put.summary: Upserts the team's capacity for one period.

get.summary: Returns the default workspace, creating it on first run.

AddFeatureDeltaRequest.description:
Adds a delta. Coverage deltas require `businessProcessId` and `toTier` (and must raise
the tier); other kinds require a `magnitude`.

AddOpportunityScopeRequest.description: Adds one business process to the scope. Scope can expand mid-cycle until the decision.

AdoptBranchRequest.description: Merges a scenario branch into the live roadmap.

BulkImportFirmsRequest.description:
Imports a roster of firms into one market. Legacy items match by natural key (market, name), so
re-importing the same roster updates rather than duplicates it; source-bound items match by
source identity (see ProductManager.Api.Contracts.FirmImportItem). An unknown segment or product fails the whole
request (404) before anything is written; identity and episode problems are per-item exceptions
that do not stop the other items.

BulkImportFirmsResponse.description:
Counters, the firms written, and one outcome per request item (same order). `firms` omits
exception items. `relationshipsWritten` counts every legacy edge and each created or updated
source-bound edge.

CalibrationParameterDiffDto.description: Prior vs posterior for one parameter, with the evidence that moved it.

CalibrationRunResultDto.description: A calibration run plus the diff it produced — what POST returns.

CalibrationUnfittedDto.description: A prior the evidence could not move, passed through with the reason why.

ChannelProductAffinityDto.description: Signed utility bias a channel applies to a product it presents. 0 is neutral.

ChannelSegmentReachDto.description:
One segment a channel touches: how much of it the channel can reach, and how much of its
opportunity flow the channel originates. Reach and origination are separate questions — a
consultant may see a whole segment yet originate nothing — and the choice engine draws an
opportunity's channel with weight reach × originationShare.

CovariateObservationDto.description: One observed value of a covariate, read back out of the bi-temporal facts ledger.

CreateCalibrationRunRequest.description:
Fits the prior assumption set to the facts ledger as it stood on `asOfDate`: only facts
recorded on or before that date are read, so a fit can honestly reconstruct what was known then.
The run is immutable and produces a new assumption set (parent = the prior, provenance
Calibrated) rather than editing the prior in place. `name` labels both the run and the
assumption set it produces; omitted, the set is named "{prior} (calibrated {asOfDate})".

CreateChannelRequest.description:
A route to market; direct sales is just another channel.
`carriesOnlyListedProducts` turns the channel's affinity list into a whitelist: products it
does not carry drop out of the consideration set of the opportunities it originates.

CreateCovariateRequest.description:
A named external time series. The three `gbm*` numbers describe the *future* path
(geometric Brownian motion, per-month log drift and volatility) and must be given together or
not at all; observed history arrives separately as facts.

CreateCoverageRequest.description:
Records a coverage assessment, upserting on the (product, process, approach?, segment?) key —
that tuple is the identity of an assessment, so posting it twice re-assesses rather than
duplicating. `isUnknown = true` records an explicit "we don't know" (distinct from
NotPlaying and from Bronze) and ignores tier/confidence.

CreateFactEventRequest.description: Appends one observation. For a covariate reading use `kind = CovariateObserved`, `subjectType = "Covariate"`, `subjectId` = the covariate, and a payload of `{"value": 1234.5}` — that is what the covariate history endpoint reads back. `recordedAt` is the import / backfill path: when history is loaded from a CRM export, a seed file or a transcript, the honest recorded date is when that observation was originally known, not when the loader ran. Omit it for a live observation and the server stamps now. It may be backdated but never post-dated — a fact cannot have been known before it was written — and `effectiveDate` rules are unchanged either way (a fact may be effective before, on, or after the date it was recorded). `source` gives the observation a source event identity, which is what tells two genuine same-day events apart from one event posted twice. A bound source record whose fact is materially identical (kind, effective date, subject, payload — notes and `recordedAt` are not material) returns that fact (200) and appends nothing; materially different is a 409 ProductManager.Api.Contracts.ProblemTypes.CorrectionRequired and appends nothing. Without `source` every call appends, as before.

CreateFirmProductRelationshipRequest.description:
`servedProcessIds` may be empty — that reads as "whatever the product covers", the honest
             state of a relationship nobody has decomposed into modules yet. `priceLevel` is a
             multiplier on list price (1.0 = list, 0.8 = a 20% discount).
            
             
`sources` makes the create repeat-safe: when any listed source record is already bound, the
             bound relationship is returned (200) and nothing is created; every listed record is bound to
             the relationship. Records bound to different relationships, or to another firm/product, are a
             409. Without `sources` every call creates, as before.

CreateIntegrationRequest.description:
A Product↔Product edge with a quality score in [0, 1]. The edge is symmetric: posting (A, B) and
(B, A) describe the same integration, and the second is rejected as a duplicate.

CreateNeedRequest.description:
A demand edge. Exactly one of `firmId` / `clientSegmentId` must be given: a need is
either one firm's or a whole segment's.

CreateOpportunityRequest.description:
Opens an opportunity: a firm seeking coverage for a scoped set of business processes.
A cross-sell is not a special case — it is an opportunity at an existing client scoped to new
processes, and `crossSellModuleProductId` names the module being sold.
            


With `source`, the create is repeat-safe: an already-bound source record returns its
opportunity (200) and creates nothing — whatever else the request says, so a retry after a lost
response is harmless; advance it with qualify/decide. A bound record whose opportunity belongs to
a different firm is a 409 ProductManager.Api.Contracts.ProblemTypes.CorrectionRequired. Without `source`
every call creates, as before.

roadmapId.description: The roadmap branch whose planned projects supply the feature coverage deltas.

assumptionSetId.description: The parameter collection the engine samples from.

horizonMonths.description: Length of the simulated horizon in months.

paths.description: Monte Carlo paths; each samples parameter uncertainty and process noise.

seed.description: Base RNG seed — the same seed and input reproduce the run exactly.

discountRateAnnual.description: Annual discount rate used to collapse margin trajectories to NPV.

terminalGrowthAnnual.description: Annual terminal growth rate for the Gordon terminal value.

name.description: Optional human label for the run.

startDate.description: Month 0 of the horizon; defaults to the first day of the current month.

marketId.description: Restricts the simulated segments to one market; omit to simulate the whole workspace.

hypotheticalEventIds.description: Hypothetical events to inject — the "what if the incident happened" arm.

CreateSimulationRunRequest.description:
Executes one simulation synchronously and stores it. The run is immutable once executed: the
engine input is snapshotted in full, so re-running the engine against the stored snapshot alone
reproduces the stored result exactly.

DecideOpportunityRequest.description:
Records the decision. `outcome` must be Won, Lost or NoDecision, and a won deal must name
the winning product (ours or a competitor's). Deciding also appends an
`OpportunityDecided` fact carrying a self-contained copy of the deal, which is what
calibration later reads — the ledger, not this row, is the history.
            

`at` is when the decision happened (the fact's effective date); `recordedAt` is when we
learned of it, and exists for the same import/backfill reason as on `POST /api/facts`:
loading last year's closed deals must not stamp them all as learned today, or every backdated
calibration reads an empty ledger. Omitted, it is stamped now; it may be backdated, never
post-dated.


Repeat-safe for every opportunity: repeating the recorded decision (same outcome, winning
product and `at` — an omitted `at` matches the recorded one) returns 200 and appends no
second fact. A different outcome, winner or date on a decided opportunity is a 409 whose
ProblemDetails `type` is ProductManager.Api.Contracts.ProblemTypes.CorrectionRequired; the opportunity and
its fact are unchanged — history is not rewritten.

DistributionSpecDto.description:
A parameter distribution: a family plus two numbers.
Point: p1 = the value, p2 must be 0. Normal: p1 = mean, p2 = std dev.
Lognormal: p1 = mu, p2 = sigma (both on the log scale). Beta: p1 = alpha, p2 = beta.

EventRateMultiplierDto.description: How an event scales one simulated flow while it is active. A null segment means all segments.

FeatureDeltaDto.description: One unit of a feature's market meaning.

FieldConflictDto.description: A source-owned field the import did not apply because it was edited locally since the last import: the stored value differs from `lastImportedValue`, and the incoming value differs from the stored one. The stored (local) value is kept. Values are canonical strings (ids as GUIDs, dates as yyyy-MM-dd, money as "1000.00 USD", lists comma-joined), null when empty.

FirmImportItem.description: One firm in a bulk import, with the relationships it already holds. Without `source` (legacy) the item is matched by (market, name) and overwrites the firm: an absent segment, attributes or notes is written as null, an absent `epistemicStatus` as Observed. With `source` the item is matched by its source binding first. A bound record updates its firm, so a changed `name` is a rename (an exception when another firm in the market has that name). An unbound record adopts the same-named firm and binds it, unless that firm is already bound to a different record of the same source system, instance and object kind — then the item is an exception ("indistinguishable same-name firms"): send a distinct, reviewed display name instead. Otherwise a new firm is created and bound. Source-bound items are partial updates. Source-owned fields: `name`, `clientSegmentId`, `epistemicStatus`, `attributesJson`, `notes`. An absent (null) field keeps the stored value; `clearFields` lists the fields to set to null (allowed: `clientSegmentId`, `attributesJson`, `notes`). A field whose stored value was edited locally since the last import (it differs from what this source last imported) is not overwritten: the item reports it under `conflicts` and keeps the local value.

FirmImportOutcomeDto.description:
Per-item result of a bulk firm import, by position in the request's `firms`. `outcome`
is about the firm row itself; its relationships report their own. Items without a
`source` report Created or Updated exactly as the counters always have.

FirmImportRelationship.description: One firm/product edge in a bulk import. Omitting an edge from a later import never ends or deletes it; `endDate` ends it. Without `sources` (legacy) the edge is matched by (firm, product) and overwritten; an absent `priceLevel` is 1.0, an absent `endDate` leaves the stored one alone. With `sources` every listed source record is bound to the one edge for (firm, product) — listing several is how records are deliberately consolidated. The model keeps one episode per edge, so these are per-item exceptions that leave the stored edge untouched: the same product twice for one firm in a request; a listed record already bound to another edge; an edge already bound to other source records none of which is listed (consolidation must be declared); a new record whose dates describe a different episode (starts after the stored end, or ends before the stored start). Source-owned fields: `acquisitionDate`, `endDate`, `pricePaidPerPeriod`, `priceLevel`, `servedProcessIds` — absent keeps, `clearFields` clears (`acquisitionDate`, `endDate`, `pricePaidPerPeriod`, `servedProcessIds`), and local edits are reported as conflicts exactly as for firms.

FirmProductRelationshipDto.description:
"Being a client" as an edge: which product, which processes it actually serves at the firm
(the modules held), what fraction of list price is paid, and when it started and ended.

GenerateSyntheticFirmsRequest.description:
Fills a market's segment stocks with deterministically generated synthetic firms. Regeneration
replaces the previous synthetic population rather than adding a second one.

ImportOutcome.description: What an import did with one item.

PagedResponseOfApproachDto.description: One page of a list endpoint's results.

PagedResponseOfAssumptionSetDto.description: One page of a list endpoint's results.

PagedResponseOfBusinessProcessDto.description: One page of a list endpoint's results.

PagedResponseOfFactEventDto.description: One page of a list endpoint's results.

PagedResponseOfFirmDto.description: One page of a list endpoint's results.

PagedResponseOfInitiativeDto.description: One page of a list endpoint's results.

PagedResponseOfIntegrationDto.description: One page of a list endpoint's results.

PagedResponseOfMarketDto.description: One page of a list endpoint's results.

PagedResponseOfMarketEventDto.description: One page of a list endpoint's results.

PlanProjectRequest.description: Plans (or re-plans) a project on the roadmap.

QualifyOpportunityRequest.description:
Qualifies an open opportunity. Repeat-safe: qualifying again at the same instant (or with
`at` omitted, once qualified) returns 200 and changes nothing; a different date on an
already-qualified opportunity is a 409 ProductManager.Api.Contracts.ProblemTypes.CorrectionRequired.

RelationshipImportOutcomeDto.description: Per-relationship result of a bulk firm import, by position in the item's `relationships`.

ReorderRoadmapRequest.description: Reorders the roadmap: sort order becomes the position in this list (the drag-and-drop reorder).

RescheduleItemRequest.description: Moves a planned project on the timeline (the drag-and-drop reschedule).

RoadmapFeasibilityDto.description: Feasibility of a roadmap: capacity overallocations and dependency-ordering problems.

SegmentApproachAdoptionDto.description: Share of a segment's firms using one alternative approach to a process.

SegmentModulePenetrationDto.description: Starting penetration and pricing of one cross-sellable module within the segment.

SegmentStockStateDto.description:
The segment's observed starting state — the stocks and unit economics the simulation engine
starts a run from. Amounts are per month in the workspace's implicit single currency.

SetEffortDemandRequest.description: Upserts the effort this project demands from one team in one period. Points of 0 clears the demand.

SetSegmentStockStateRequest.description: Replaces the segment's whole starting state — it is one measurement, not a set of knobs.

SetTeamCapacityRequest.description: Upserts a team's capacity for one period. Points are FTE-months or story points — a unit choice made in data.

SourceBindingDto.description:
One source record and the row it became. `targetType` is Firm, Opportunity,
FirmProductRelationship or FactEvent. `importedValuesJson` is the source-owned field values
as last imported (field → value), which is what local-edit conflicts are detected against.

SourceRef.description:
Identity of one record in an external source system, e.g.
`{"sourceSystem":"salesforce","sourceInstance":"acme.my.salesforce.com","objectKind":"Account","sourceRecordId":"001…"}`.
Free strings — import metadata, never a list of vendors — compared exactly (case-sensitive,
untrimmed). A source record is bound to exactly one domain row per workspace; binding the same
key to a second row is refused.

TokenRequest.description: Single-user sign-in: the shared password from configuration.

TokenResponse.description: A bearer token to send as `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`.

UpdateCoverageRequest.description: Re-assesses an existing coverage row found by id; the key dimensions are immutable.

UpdateFirmProductRelationshipRequest.description:
Replaces the whole edge. Omitting `endDate` reopens a relationship that had ended — a PUT
states what is true now, and "no end date" means "still a client".

UpsertParameterRequest.description: Sets (upserting) one parameter. Give `clientSegmentId` + `flowKind` (+ `moduleProductId` for CrossSellRate) to write a parameter the engine reads — those three are the engine's own parameter key, so writing the same triple twice replaces rather than duplicates. Give `key` instead for a free-form assumption the engine ignores. `covariateBeta` is an elasticity: the engine applies rate_t = rate * (x_t / x_0)^beta, so +1% on the covariate is about +beta% on the rate. The covariate's units are irrelevant (the term is a ratio), but its path must be strictly positive wherever beta is nonzero.

tags.name: AssumptionSets
tags.description:
Versioned, branchable parameter collections. Every parameter carries a distribution, a
provenance (asserted / calibrated / default) and a rationale — "what if churn is 2×" is a
one-parameter branch, not an edit that quietly rewrites what past runs were executed against.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Single-user sign-in. Phase 1 has one shared password and one bearer token.

tags.name: CalibrationRuns
tags.description: Immutable fits: the prior assumption set plus the facts ledger as of a date produce a new, fitted assumption set, diffable against the prior. The as-of cut is the whole point. Only facts whose `recordedDate` falls on or before the date are read, so a fit reconstructs what was actually known then rather than quietly borrowing hindsight — which is the difference between a backtest and a flattering story about one. A fit never edits the prior: it creates a branch whose fitted parameters carry provenance Calibrated and an auto-generated rationale naming the evidence ("fitted from 42 decided opportunities"), so every number stays traceable to what moved it.

tags.name: Facts
tags.description:
The bi-temporal facts ledger: every market observation, with when it was true and when we
learned it. Append-only by construction — there is no update and no delete, because rewriting
history is exactly what would make "what we knew as of date D" a lie.

tags.name: Covariates
tags.description:
Named external time series that drive flows — an equity index, a rate, a volume. Observed
history lives in the facts ledger; the future is a scenario spec sampled per Monte Carlo path.

tags.name: Features
tags.description:
Product capabilities (not work items). A feature's market meaning is its set of deltas —
mostly coverage deltas ("bronze → gold on process P for segment S").

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Liveness probe. Anonymous so clients can check the API before they hold a token.

tags.name: Initiatives
tags.description: Strategic bets — the *why*. Initiatives contain Projects and target market-side segments and needs.

tags.name: Markets
tags.description:
Competitive arenas. Phase 1 exposes create/read only — the full market UX arrives in Phase 2 —
but the API is the only write path, so the CLI seeds market data through these endpoints.

tags.name: ClientSegments
tags.description: Groups of firms with a shared profile.

tags.name: BusinessProcesses
tags.description: The catalog of what firms must accomplish — the vocabulary demand and supply both point at.

tags.name: Approaches
tags.description: Alternative methods for a business process (the nullable approach dimension).

tags.name: Competitors
tags.description: Organizations owning rival products.

tags.name: Products
tags.description: Sellable offerings, ours or a competitor's. A module is a product with a parent product.

tags.name: Coverages
tags.description:
Supply assessments: (Product × BusinessProcess × Approach? × Segment?) → tier.
Unknown is recorded explicitly — it is not the same as bronze.

tags.name: Firms
tags.description:
Market participants: prospects, our clients, competitors' clients, and synthetic firms generated
to fill the unobserved market. The epistemic status says which kind of knowledge a row is.

tags.name: Needs
tags.description:
The demand edge: what a firm — or a whole segment — must accomplish, how much it matters, and
what the workaround costs when it goes unmet.

tags.name: MarketEvents
tags.description:
Typed shocks that modulate simulated flows for a duration. Real events mirror the facts ledger;
hypothetical ones are injected into a scenario — "with the incident" vs "without".

tags.name: Opportunities
tags.description:
The central hinge of the market model: a firm seeking coverage for a scoped set of business
processes. Scope can expand mid-cycle (land-and-expand); the lifecycle is open → qualified →
decided (won / lost / no-decision), and "no decision" is a real outcome rather than a missing one.
            


Deciding an opportunity also appends an ProductManager.Domain.Common.FactEventKind.OpportunityDecided entry to
the bi-temporal ledger, carrying a self-contained copy of the deal. Calibration reads that
ledger, never these rows: a fit "as of date D" must see what was recorded by D, and an
opportunity row keeps changing afterwards.

tags.name: Channels
tags.description:
Routes to market: reach into segments, opportunity origination, per-product bias. Direct sales
is just another channel — there is no special-case "direct" entity, and an opportunity with no
channel is simply unrouted.

tags.name: Integrations
tags.description:
Product↔Product edges with a quality score, including integrations with partial competitors.
They are what makes a best-of-breed choice rational: a candidate is judged partly on how well it
fits the stack a firm already runs.

tags.name: FirmRelationships
tags.description:
"Being a client" as an edge: firm holds product, serving these processes, at this share of list
price, from this date. The same shape carries competitors' client relationships — which is what
makes an incumbent's position measurable rather than assumed.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description:
Units of execution: dates, per-team per-period effort demand, dependencies, and the seam
(a project delivers features).

tags.name: Roadmaps
tags.description:
Branchable, versioned plans. The live roadmap is a living document; a scenario is a branch
(deep copy of the plan links) and adopting a scenario is a merge back into the live roadmap.

tags.name: SimulationRuns
tags.description:
Immutable simulation executions. A run references a roadmap branch, an assumption set, a
covariate scenario, an event overlay and a seed, snapshots the resulting engine input in full,
and stores the trajectories. Runs are never mutated — only created, read and deleted — because
comparing two runs is only honest if neither has changed underneath you.

tags.name: SourceBindings
tags.description:
Import provenance, read-only: which source record became which row. Bindings are written by the
import paths themselves (firm bulk import, opportunity/relationship/fact creates with a source);
this listing is what an importer resolves and plans against, and what reconciliation traces a
row back to its source record with.

tags.name: Teams
tags.description:
Capacity budget units. No per-person allocation and no skills model — a team's capacity per
period is a feasibility constraint checked against roadmap effort demand.

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description: The root aggregate. Phase 1 auto-creates a single default workspace on first use.
